> As I've mentioned in the proposal, I am not opposed to implementing this, but I feel more improvements are necessary
> 
> * Regarding SyncMode naming, it should use "Independent" instead of "Discrete", and "Phase" or "Cyclic" instead of “Continuous”
> * Performing division every frame is costly, so I believe we need to cache the divided values per point and perform simple addition instead. You can refer AnimatedSprite time progression process
> * In addition to runtime warnings, clearer preventive measures are needed, such as displaying a popup warning in the Animation Tree Editor (similar to the Animation Player's ReadOnly warning) or marking points with "×" if the point is **not** AnimationNodeAnimation
>

> A weighted-average period is computed from the active blend points:

Also I think this should be implemented by allowing any length to be specified for the BlendSpace when SyncMode is set to Cyclic similar with NodeAnimation's CustomTimeline length. After that, you can add buttons to calculate automatically and input statically the average, max or min values as options in the Editor.

Cases where the average should be calculated dynamically refer to situations where the number of animations under the BlendSpace changes at runtime, but such cases should be rare.

At this point this is getting pretty complex right? I mean I've been at this a while and if animations are that far out of wack your looking at reauthoring or offsetting the timeline which we already have tools for???? The above implimentation is essentially how other engines handle it .... minus say Unreal's Sync Marker system. Shouldn't we just handle the basic requested proposal first and then we can expand on that? It looks like this first part will handle the bulk of what people are really wanting and put godot in line for the most part. I will happily expand on this in the future :)

Auto calculation option can be added later to Editor. The only request here is to let the BlendSpace has a single double property like `cyclic_length` and uses it, instead of calculating retrieving the avg_length at runtime from all animations within the BlendSpace.

> Auto calculation option can be added later to Editor. The only request here is to have the BlendSpace has a single double property like `cyclic_length` and uses it, instead of calculating retrieving the avg_length at runtime from all animations within the BlendSpace.

Meaning an overriding it instead of the optimization??
Animation lengths can be cached in `cached_lengths[]` and only recomputed when blend points are added, removed, or replaced (`lengths_dirty` flag). Per-frame math computes a single reciprocal of the weighted-average length (`inv_avg_length = total_weight / weighted_length_sum`) and then uses multiplication (`cached_lengths[i] * inv_avg_length`) instead of per-point division. This follows the same pattern as `AnimatedSprite2D::_calc_frame_speed_scale()`. 

Don't you think this would be better than having someone manually figure out the avg_length()???

Also if an override is provided then sure your not needing to worry about runtime animation changes but at least with this implementation it's still possible to just setup and go and let the method do the work vs recalculate for every anim blend in code?

For example, suppose we have the following animation:

```
A: 1s
B: 2s
C: 3s
```

With your method, BlendSpace automatically calculates the average and sets 2s as one cycle length.

I'm simply saying we should allow manual input for the cycle length. For example, if the cycle length is set to 5s, the following double values would be cached for each point:

```
A_delta_factor: 1/5=0.2
B_delta_factor: 2/5=0.4
C_delta_factor: 3/5=0.6
```

After this, time progression can be handled as follows:

```
N_pos += N_delta_factor * animation_mixer_delta
```

Ah I see... will work on this .. I was thinking to add cyclic_length as a property with default 0.0 meaning "auto-compute from blend point lengths". When it's 0, do what is in (weighted average from cached lengths). When the user sets it > 0, use their override. This gives both behaviors, and keeps the "just works" default

Side note I see you keep using cyclic instead of SYNC_MODE_PHASE ... are you not ok with this... would you prefer me use cyclic instead?

> When it's 0, do what is in (weighted average from cached lengths).

Since the user's intent regarding whether the auto-calculation should be the average, maximum, or minimum depends on the user (Unreal choosed minimum length AFAIR), I think making this a proprietary feature is not a good idea. Therefore, I recommended above to simply treat 0 as an invalid value (or disallow input) and add an editor option later.

Ah, I understand. You mean that when blending a 1-second animation and a 2-second animation, you also want the cycle length to change between 1 and 2 seconds. In that case, I think the Enum should have four values. 0 check is probably bit more expensive than ENUM match and they have no needed double member.

- SYNC_MODE_NONE
- SYNC_MODE_INDEPENDENT
- SYNC_MODE_CYCLIC_MUTABLE
- SYNC_MODE_CYCLIC_CONSTANT

In any case, pre-divided values are required for each point. Then time progression should be done for `SYNC_MODE_CYCLIC_MUTABLE`:

```
-- members --
A_len: 1s
B_len: 2s
C_len: 3s
-- when blend value changed (cached) --
N_delta_factor = N_len/blended_len
-- each frame --
N_pos += N_delta_factor * animation_mixer_delta
```

And I beieve, you will likely need to add them to AnimationNodeSync as well, not just AnimationNodeBlendSpace.

I simply see an issue with this approach.....

With the old auto-calculation, when only one animation had weight (e.g., idle at 100%), the weighted average equaled that animation's own length:

avg_length = idle_length * 1.0 / 1.0 = idle_length
delta_factor = idle_length / idle_length = 1.0 — no speed change
With a static [cyclic_length] if your idle is (say) 2.0s and you set [cyclic_length = 1.0s]

delta_factor = 2.0 / 1.0 = 2.0 — idle plays 2x fast, even when it's the only active animation

this isn't really user preference unless they want to avg all animations across the length override then sure.... also the other methods I'm mentioning aren't "proprietary" its just handling blending per cycles based on delta_factor ... unity, unreal, source and many others all have this?

See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117275#issuecomment-4028373831 despite the time lag. I request that the pre-division result cache be made mandatory, that it be implemented as four Enums.

And that the same approach be applied to AnimationNodeSync if you can (BTW you can ignore StateMachine's Sync transition for now. It has fundamental issues and needs to be reworked). However, since it seems difficult to issue warnings in AnimationNodeSync, focusing solely on BlendSpace for now is acceptable.
